top_choice_rationale: Cărtărescu (P001) remains my first choice on the common criteria. On public knowledge, which I have not independently verified, the Blinding trilogy and Solenoid make memory, the body and dream the structural principle of very large books. Voice, formal ambition and imaginative depth appear to be one thing, and the project reads as cumulative from a poetic foundation, which bears on sustained quality. The citation should rest on the prose cycles, with poetry named only as ground. The reservations are real: the judgment is made through translation, and I cannot confirm that the late long novels are evenly sustained. Carson (P003) is second because her voice and formal invention are directly legible in English, and Sward's continuity argument answers the signal-books worry. A text-only citation must carry the claim without relying on book-object form. Adonis (P002) is third because his remaking of Arabic poetic language is a serious achievement, but the committee can judge it only through translation and secondhand accounts, and the later poetry is unverified. This is an evidentiary limit, not a verdict on his standing. P000 is last because none of the three leading cases is so thin that withholding the prize is warranted. Support counts and the four-vote threshold are not merit and were given no weight.
